title: Offline Multi-agent Continual Cooperation via Skill Partition and Reuse
claim: A continual multi-agent skill-learning setting, its modular actor architecture, and the key principles behind it form one coherent system.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right; dotted gray arrows link architecture to principles
description: A wide three-panel figure with a labeled caption under each panel. Panel (a), the multi-agent task stream, shows a task stream on a gray background. The left side has Venn diagrams and distribution sketches for new skills and new scenarios. The middle has agent-team icons. The right side has stacked mini-plots for Task 1, Task 2 and Task m, which feed into a dataset cylinder along a timeline arrow. Panel (b), the actor architecture, is a block diagram with Prior, Encoder and Confidence modules built on GRU, MLP and self-attention layers. These feed an Action Decoder, and red loss terms (policy, KL, NCE, L2) are marked on top. Panel (c) shows the three key principles: behavior decoupling, shown as skill-prior histograms and a theoretical-optimal curve, and reusability estimation, shown as colored confidence boxes on a 0–1 axis. Both are connected by double arrows to formulas. Red, blue and purple color-code old skills, new skills and mixed skills. The eye goes first to panel (b)'s dense diagram.
caption: An illustration of our method COMAD. (a) Given a multi-agent task stream, the continual agents must discover skills from offline data of different tasks sequentially, where two types of distribution shift occur. (b) COMAD actor is equipped with multi-headed architectures to overcome the challenge of emerging skills by encoding and decoding skills from different scenarios, meanwhile estimating their reusability for efficient transfer. (c) The key principles of COMAD for continual skill discovery include decoupling behaviors from mixed datasets and selectively reuse them based on reusability.
abstract: Extracting skills from multi-agent offline dataset improves learning efficiency via sharing task-invariant coordination skills among tasks. In settings where tasks occur sequentially and the space of skills grows exponentially, existing approaches that rely on heuristically designed and fixed-sized skill libraries struggle to resolve the problem of distributional shift and interference, facing catastrophic forgetting and plasticity loss. To address this problem and endow agents with the ability to continually discover and reuse coordination skills in open-environment, we propose COMAD, a principled framework for Continual Offline Multi-agent Skill Discovery via Skill Partition and Reuse. We first discover skills from mixed multi-agent behavior data with an auto-encoder to transform coordination knowledge into reusable coordination skills. Then we construct a skill-augmented policy learning objective with multi-head architectures, explicitly guiding the advantage function with reusable skills identified via a density-based reusability estimator. Theoretical analysis shows our method approximates the optimum of a continual skill discovery problem. Empirical results across diverse MARL benchmarks show that COMAD continually expands its skill library to mitigate interference, achieving superior forward and backward transfer for task streams compared to multiple baselines.
